newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were little changed in quiet trade on Thursday with relatively tight ARA supplies balancing the market against volatile NYMEX unleaded, traders said.
Barge and cargo prices talked in a slightly wider range with a shortage of fixed offers for cargoes and regional holiday in Germany dampening demand for barges.
Traders said arbitrage opportunities to the United States were not considered workable because of the lack of cargo-sized pieces in Northwest Europe.
Prompt lifting Eurograde barges were talked around $203/$205 fob ARA with trade at $204 for a June 1-15 lifting fob AR.
Regular valued slightly firmer at $197 and thinly talked superplus around $205 a tonne.

Eurograde cargo talk was thin, prices initially edge up on the back of firmer U.S. spot markets to value around $215 a tonne cif NWE. But weakness on NYMEX unleaded shaved the gains, leaving prices unchanged around $213.
Wednesday's API report showing U.S. gasoline stocks off 1.1 million barrels and down around eight million barrels from this time last year was largely shrugged off by the markets.
The report said RFG stocks rose 1.35 million barrels last week.
